root_cause.text: A race in the UFS core suspend path (__ufshcd_wl_suspend()) left hba->ufs_rtc_update_work active until after ufshcd_vops_suspend(), allowing ufshcd_rtc_work() to access/update UFS hardware while vendor suspend clock-gating was in progress.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves cancel_delayed_work_sync(&hba->ufs_rtc_update_work) from after the suspend sequence to before ufshcd_vops_suspend(hba, pm_op, PRE_CHANGE), and the CVE/commit explicitly states this ordering let ufshcd_rtc_work() run concurrently with ufshcd_vops_suspend(), causing ufshcd_update_rtc() to trigger an SError during clock gating.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending UFS RTC update delayed work during suspend to avoid races with the suspend sequence.
intent_record.what: A call to cancel_delayed_work_sync(&hba->ufs_rtc_update_work) was added in __ufshcd_wl_suspend() immediately after flush_work(&hba->eeh_work) and before ufshcd_vops_suspend(hba, pm_op, PRE_CHANGE).
intent_record.how: At suspend time, the driver now synchronously cancels any pending or running delayed ufs_rtc_update_work before proceeding with vendor suspend operations, preventing that work item from executing during or after the suspend transition and avoiding suspend-time races or invalid access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unnecessary cancellation of RTC update delayed work during successful UFS suspend to avoid incorrect suspend-time work handling.
intent_record.what: The call to cancel_delayed_work_sync(&hba->ufs_rtc_update_work) was removed from the successful path of __ufshcd_wl_suspend() just before jumping to the out label.
intent_record.how: On a successful suspend flow, the driver no longer synchronously cancels the delayed RTC update work at this point, allowing that work item to remain scheduled or be handled elsewhere instead of being forcibly stopped during suspend.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it cancels the pending UFS RTC update work during suspend, preventing ufshcd_rtc_work() from running while vendor suspend/clock-gating is in progress.

The change directly modifies how the RTC update delayed work is handled during UFS suspend. Since the root cause is a suspend-path race involving hba->ufs_rtc_update_work remaining active around vendor suspend clock-gating, a patch that removes or alters cancellation of that RTC work during successful suspend is directly tied to the vulnerable logic.

candidates.rationale: This shows the RTC update work was only being cancelled later in the suspend path, after earlier suspend operations. That timing matches the root cause: the work remained active until after vendor suspend handling began, allowing a race with hardware access during clock-gating.

This vendor suspend callback was reached before the RTC delayed work was cancelled. As a result, vendor-specific suspend and clock-gating could proceed while ufshcd_rtc_work() was still runnable, creating the race described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This vendor suspend callback was executed before the RTC delayed work was cancelled. That ordering allowed hba->ufs_rtc_update_work to remain active while vendor suspend clock-gating was in progress, matching the race described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the suspend sequencing around the vendor suspend callbacks. The root cause says `hba->ufs_rtc_update_work` remained active until after `ufshcd_vops_suspend()`, allowing RTC work to touch hardware while vendor suspend clock-gating was in progress. In this function, before calling the vendor pre-suspend callback at line 8847 (`ret = ufshcd_vops_suspend(hba, pm_op, PRE_CHANGE);`), the code only flushes `eeh_work` at line 8845 (`flush_work(&hba->eeh_work);`). There is no flush/cancel of `hba->ufs_rtc_update_work` anywhere in the shown function. Since the vulnerable construct is the lack of draining RTC update work before vendor suspend, that vulnerable condition is present here. Therefore `has_bug=true`. The fix is not present because the function does not stop or flush RTC update work before either `ufshcd_vops_suspend(..., PRE_CHANGE)` or `ufshcd_vops_suspend(..., POST_CHANGE)`; it only handles `eeh_work`. Thus `is_fixed=false`.
